name: Stein Eriksen Lodge Deer Valley
positioning: Norwegian-style ski lodge set mid-mountain at Deer Valley Resort in Park City, Utah, inspired by Olympic skier Stein Eriksen
best_for: Skiers who want a mid-mountain base at Deer Valley Resort
Summer hikers and mountain bikers who want to step straight onto lift-served trails
Families and groups who want multi-bedroom suites

facts.text: The lodge is located mid-mountain at Deer Valley Resort in Park City, Utah, with direct access to skiing.
The lodge is approximately five minutes from Historic Main Street Park City.
The lodge is furnished with oversized leather chairs and crackling fireplaces.
Each Lodge Luxury Bedroom is unique in style, configuration and decor, so no two rooms are identical.
Each Lodge Luxury Suite is individually decorated with one to five bedrooms, and most include a private deck and hot tub.
Suites come with large stone fireplaces.
Spa facilities include indoor hot and cold plunge pools, steam rooms and a dry sauna.
Stein Eriksen Sport, on the main level of the lodge, rents bikes and equipment.
Champions Club is a family entertainment center with complimentary arcade games.
The lodge's wine collection tops 20,000 bottles and over 2,100 selections.
Troll Hallen Lounge is the lodge's apres-ski spot, with cocktails, small plates and mountain views.

highlights.text: Inspired by Olympic legend Stein Eriksen and his Norwegian heritage, the traditional ski lodge was the first luxury property in Park City.
The Norwegian-style lodge has custom millwork, flower paintings from the lowland areas of eastern Norway, and leather, copper and stone elements.
At least 80 percent of rooms have a fireplace, and all rooms have large soaking tubs.
Next to the spa and fitness center is an outdoor space with two heated pools and two hot tubs, open year-round to spa guests.
Guests can step directly from the lodge onto lift-served hiking and biking trails at Deer Valley Resort.

considerations.text: Access to the spa facilities, including the outdoor pools, is included with spa treatments of $100 or more.
For ski-in, ski-out access, most guests use the ski locker area.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing year-round.
